about: Which selftests a changed file can affect (product rule 8). bin/test-map.py reads this: `check` is the lint (in npm test through bin/test-map-selftest.sh), `select` picks the targets. The map is finished: every tracked file has a row whose targets are the selftests that use it (from reach, or from reading, said in the row's why; "unsure: the folder's tests" where no use was found), and `check` refuses a tracked file no row matches. The full list ships empty: it stays in the schema and the tool for a stack that wants one (a file on it selects the full suite). The full suite runs once, at the end, on the final hash. `check` refuses a map whose rows leave out a selftest that can reach the file (see reach in bin/test-map.py); the error names what to add. `scan` rows are for selftests that read a whole folder; every glob of any other row starts with a literal folder or top-level file name (no wildcard in the first path component), so a file under a name no row spells selects the full suite. A row that, for a file, adds no target beyond the always gates and the scan rows matching it may match only prose: no code, executable, test-like file (its gate's own selftest and tool excepted), or file a code or data file (`data`; empty means every file) names. Removing a glob from `data` loosens that rule, and `check` accepts it (a known limit: nothing forces a review of such an edit; what holds is that every edit of this map runs `check`). This map, its schema and bin/test-map.py select their users like any other file, and `select` adds the tool's own selftest, which runs `check`, to every narrow answer whatever this map says. `select` answers full only for an input or a map it cannot trust: a name no row matches or that is not one plain file name, no name, names it cannot read, a map, schema or tool module that is missing, unreadable or broken, a map that breaks a rule needing no file list, an empty selection.
